precepts.text: The stone which the builders refused is become the head stone of the corner; the headstone Zerubbabel brings forth is the same stone laid before Joshua.
precepts.point: Behold, I will bring forth my servant the Branch, and the stone laid before Joshua with seven eyes; the Branch and the stone are Christ.

note.label: The Nativity: the Bloodline, Birthright, & the Messiah

precepts.why:
Zechariah says, “For behold the stone that I have laid before Joshua; upon one stone shall be seven eyes.” The Branch and the stone are Christ. Then Zerubbabel “shall bring forth the headstone thereof.”

What is the headstone? “The stone which the builders refused is become the head stone of the corner.” Who is the Branch, who is the stone? It's the same thing. The headstone Zerubbabel brings forth is the same stone laid before Joshua, and the same servant the Branch the Lord said he would bring forth: Christ, refused by the builders and made the head of the corner.

So when the Lord says “I will remove the iniquity of that land in one day”, he is going into Christ. The stone laid before Joshua the high priest and his fellows, men wondered at for a sign, is the Christ who would come through Zerubbabel's loins.

precepts.text: The stone which the builders refused is become the head stone of the corner. Who is that, brothers? That is Christ; he is the headstone.
precepts.point: The hands of Zerubbabel have laid the foundation of this house; his hands shall also finish it. His hands started the foundation of the temple, and he did finish the temple. However, this goes deeper than that: verses 6 through 9 are also going into the last days.

note.label: We Are Born in Babylon

precepts.why:
Zerubbabel is the branch in the line of Christ: Matthew's genealogy runs from Zerubbabel through Abiud, Eliakim, Azor, Sadoc, Achim, Eliud, Eleazar, Matthan and Jacob to “Joseph the husband of Mary, of whom was born Jesus, who is called Christ.” So when the Lord speaks to Zerubbabel, he is speaking to the father of Christ's line.

“Not by might, nor by power, but by my spirit, saith the Lord of hosts.” Zerubbabel was of the king's bodyguard, one of the top fighters. The Lord is telling him, no, this has nothing to do with your fighting skills; we know you can break bones, but that's not what is going to overcome everything. The spirit of the Lord is what's going to do it.

“Who art thou, O great mountain? before Zerubbabel thou shalt become a plain.” The great mountain is Babylon the great, and it shall become a plain: flattened, destroyed. “and he shall bring forth the headstone thereof with shoutings, crying, Grace, grace unto it”: crying mercy, mercy unto it.

What is the headstone? “The stone which the builders refused is become the head stone of the corner.” Who is that? Christ. He is the headstone. Not only would Christ come from Zerubbabel's lineage; Zerubbabel shall bring forth the headstone.

“The hands of Zerubbabel have laid the foundation of this house; his hands shall also finish it.” His hands started the foundation of the temple, and he did finish the temple. But this goes deeper than that: because of verse 7, verses 6 through 9 are going into the last days as well, when the great mountain, Babylon the great, is brought down to a plain and the headstone, Christ, is brought forth.

precepts.text: Concerning the prophets that make my people err: night shall be unto you, that ye shall not have a vision, and the sun shall go down over the prophets. The darkness on the rulers means they could no longer teach, so today they run to the white man's theology schools.
precepts.point: The stone which the builders refused is become the head stone of the corner; this is the Lord's doing. Not all Jews refused him: the builders refused him, and it was the Lord's doing, so that their rejection would have him killed and bring the northern kingdom back in.

note.label: The Dividing Hatred: the Grafted in Strangers

precepts.why:
“The stone which the builders refused” is refused by the builders, the rulers, because they were in darkness. Micah shows the darkness God put on them: “Thus saith the Lord concerning the prophets that make my people err, that bite with their teeth, and cry, Peace; and he that putteth not into their mouths, they even prepare war against him.” They prepare war against us, because they are teaching the wrong thing.

“Therefore night shall be unto you”. He is talking to the prophets, the elders. Night goes back to darkness, your eyes being closed. If you can't see, you start stumbling; you don't know where you're going, you're falling. That is the stone of stumbling at work.

It goes on, “that ye shall not have a vision”: your eyes are closed, you can't read the Bible no more, you can't teach the Bible no more. God stops talking to you entirely. Then “it shall be dark unto you, that ye shall not divine”: you cannot teach correctly. So now you go to theology school and run to the white man for help: Mr. White Man, can you teach me the Bible, please? Can I go to your school and learn BS, please?

Then “the sun shall go down over the prophets, and the day shall be dark over them.” The sun going down means dark: no understanding. The light is taken from them and they lose understanding.

That is why the builders refused the stone. And it was the Lord's doing: the builders rejecting him so that they would have him killed, and so bring in the northern kingdom, whereunto they were appointed. Not all Israel refused him; the builders did. And he that was refused “is become the head stone of the corner”: he becomes our king and ruler in the end.

precepts.text: The stone which the builders refused is become the head stone of the corner.
precepts.point: They are drunken, but not with wine; the Lord hath closed your eyes, the prophets and seers hath he covered.

note.label: All Skinfolk Ain't Kinfolk: Children of Darkness

precepts.why:
“they are drunken, but not with wine; they stagger, but not with strong drink. For the Lord hath poured out upon you the spirit of deep sleep, and hath closed your eyes: the prophets and your rulers, the seers hath he covered.” Covered what? Their eyes. They were evil and rebellious back then, and evil and rebellious now.

David shows who they rejected: “The stone which the builders refused is become the head stone of the corner.” The builders are the rulers: the elders, the Pharisees, the scribes, whose eyes the Lord covered in darkness because they were wicked as hell. The stone they refused is Christ.

That is why Christ could ask them, “What is this then that is written, The stone which the builders rejected”: he was speaking the parable against them. The husbandmen beat the servants and killed the heir, and the rulers knew he was talking about them. They were drunk, but not with wine; their eyes were darkened, and so the builders refused the head stone of the corner, the black Messiah.

precepts.text: Fear not them which kill the body but are not able to kill the soul, but rather fear Him which is able to destroy both soul and body in hell.
precepts.point: I called upon the Lord in distress and He answered me and set me in a large place. The Lord is on my side; I will not fear what man can do unto me, but this does not mean fear will never come upon you at all.

note.label: Psalm 118: His Mercy Endureth For Ever

precepts.why:
“The Lord is on my side; I will not fear: what can man do unto me?” This does not mean fear will never come upon you at all. Christ puts fear in its place: “fear not them which kill the body, but are not able to kill the soul: but rather fear him which is able to destroy both soul and body in hell.”

Man can only kill the body. The one to fear is the Most High, who is able to destroy both soul and body in hell. With the Lord on our side, what man can do unto us is nothing to fear.

precepts.text: The young men despised the pains and died for the laws of the Most High, showing the very spirit of not fearing them that kill the body.
precepts.point: I called upon the Lord in distress and He answered me and set me in a large place. The Lord is on my side; I will not fear what man can do unto me, but this does not mean fear will never come upon you at all.

note.label: Psalm 118: His Mercy Endureth For Ever

precepts.why:
“what can man do unto me?” The brothers in 2 Maccabees show the very spirit of it. One “said courageously, These I had from heaven; and for his laws I despise them; and from him I hope to receive them again.”

“Insomuch that the king, and they that were with him, marvelled at the young man’s courage, for that he nothing regarded the pains.” Then the fourth, when he was ready to die: “It is good, being put to death by men, to look for hope from God to be raised up again by him: as for thee, thou shalt have no resurrection to life.”

The young men despised the pains and died for the laws of the Most High, not fearing them that kill the body. The Lord was on their side, and man could only put them to death, with the hope of being raised up again by God.

precepts.text: My son, if thou come to serve the Lord, prepare thy soul for temptation, set thy heart aright, endure, and take whatever is brought upon thee cheerfully, for gold is tried in the fire and acceptable men in the furnace of adversity.
precepts.point: The Lord has chastened me sore but has not given me over unto death. When you come to serve the Lord, understand that this walk brings chastising to try us.

note.label: Psalm 118: His Mercy Endureth For Ever

precepts.why:
“The Lord hath chastened me sore: but he hath not given me over unto death.” When you come to serve the Lord, understand that this walk brings chastising to try us. “My son, if thou come to serve the Lord, prepare thy soul for temptation. Set thy heart aright, and constantly endure, and make not haste in time of trouble.”

“Cleave unto him, and depart not away, that thou mayest be increased at thy last end. Whatsoever is brought upon thee take cheerfully, and be patient when thou art changed to a low estate.” Whatever is brought upon you, take it cheerfully.

“For gold is tried in the fire, and acceptable men in the furnace of adversity.” The chastening is the furnace; it tries us as gold is tried, and it does not give us over unto death. So the righteous can still say, I shall not die, but live, and declare the works of the Lord.

precepts.text: By the word of truth, by honor and dishonor, as chastened and not killed; the prophets and the apostle Paul agree with what we read in the psalm.
precepts.point: The Lord has chastened me sore but has not given me over unto death. When you come to serve the Lord, understand that this walk brings chastising to try us.

note.label: Psalm 118: His Mercy Endureth For Ever

precepts.why:
“By the word of truth, by the power of God, by the armour of righteousness on the right hand and on the left, By honour and dishonour, by evil report and good report: as deceivers, and yet true; As unknown, and yet well known; as dying, and, behold, we live; as chastened, and not killed”.

“as chastened, and not killed” is the psalm word for word in the apostle's mouth: “The Lord hath chastened me sore: but he hath not given me over unto death.” “as dying, and, behold, we live” is “I shall not die, but live”. The prophets and the apostle Paul agree with what we read in the psalm: this walk brings honour and dishonour, evil report and good report, chastening but not death.

precepts.text: The husbandmen killed the heir and cast him out, so the lord of the vineyard will destroy them; the stone which the builders rejected is become the head of the corner.
precepts.point: The stone which the builders refused is become the head stone of the corner; this is the Lord's doing and it is marvelous in our eyes. This is prophecy speaking of Christ, showing that Christ is in the Old Testament.

note.label: Psalm 118: His Mercy Endureth For Ever

precepts.why:
“The stone which the builders refused is become the head stone of the corner. This is the Lord’s doing; it is marvellous in our eyes.” This is prophecy speaking of Christ, and Christ himself applies it. “But those husbandmen said among themselves, This is the heir; come, let us kill him, and the inheritance shall be ours. And they took him, and killed him, and cast him out of the vineyard.”

“What shall therefore the lord of the vineyard do? he will come and destroy the husbandmen, and will give the vineyard unto others.” Then Christ asks, “And have ye not read this scripture; The stone which the builders rejected is become the head of the corner: This was the Lord’s doing, and it is marvellous in our eyes?”

The heir the husbandmen killed and cast out is the stone the builders refused, and he is become the head of the corner. Christ is in the Old Testament, and he read this psalm of himself.

precepts.text: Lo, I come, in the volume of the book it is written of Me, showing that Christ is written of in the Old Testament.
precepts.point: The stone which the builders refused is become the head stone of the corner; this is the Lord's doing and it is marvelous in our eyes. This is prophecy speaking of Christ, showing that Christ is in the Old Testament.

note.label: Psalm 118: His Mercy Endureth For Ever

precepts.why:
“Then said I, Lo, I come (in the volume of the book it is written of me,) to do thy will, O God.” Christ is written of in the volume of the book, the Old Testament.

That is what the psalm is: the stone which the builders refused becoming the head stone of the corner is written of him. He came to do the Father's will as it was written, and this is the Lord's doing, marvellous in our eyes.

precepts.text: The multitudes cried Hosanna to the son of David, blessed is he that cometh in the name of the Lord, and the multitude said this is Jesus of Nazareth, the Messiah spoken of in the psalm.
precepts.point: God is the Lord which has showed us light. The light is the laws, and we are to bind the sacrifice with cords unto the horns of the altar and give thanks unto the Lord, for He is good and His mercy endures forever unto the children of the promise.

note.label: Psalm 118: His Mercy Endureth For Ever

precepts.why:
“Blessed be he that cometh in the name of the Lord: we have blessed you out of the house of the Lord.” The multitudes said it to Christ as he came into Jerusalem: “Hosanna to the Son of David: Blessed is he that cometh in the name of the Lord; Hosanna in the highest.”

“And when he was come into Jerusalem, all the city was moved, saying, Who is this? And the multitude said, This is Jesus the prophet of Nazareth of Galilee.” The one that cometh in the name of the Lord in the psalm is Jesus of Nazareth, the Messiah spoken of here. This is the day which the Lord hath made.

precepts.text: The commandment is a lamp and the law is light, so the light showed us is the laws of the Most High.
precepts.point: God is the Lord which has showed us light. The light is the laws, and we are to bind the sacrifice with cords unto the horns of the altar and give thanks unto the Lord, for He is good and His mercy endures forever unto the children of the promise.

note.label: Psalm 118: His Mercy Endureth For Ever

precepts.why:
“God is the Lord, which hath shewed us light”. The light is the laws: “For the commandment is a lamp; and the law is light; and reproofs of instruction are the way of life”.

The light he has shewed us is the laws of the Most High. Having that light, we bind the sacrifice with cords unto the horns of the altar and give thanks unto the Lord, for he is good, and his mercy endureth for ever unto the children of the promise.

precepts.text: Open to me the gates of righteousness; that gate of the Most High into which the righteous shall enter is the straight gate.
precepts.point: The gates are opened that the righteous nation which keepeth the truth may enter in, and that nation is the remnant that keeps the commandments. Whose mind is stayed on the Most High is kept in perfect peace because he trusteth in Him.

note.label: Isaiah 26: A Song of Salvation and the Straight Gate

precepts.why:
“Open ye the gates, that the righteous nation which keepeth the truth may enter in.” David asks for those same gates: “Open to me the gates of righteousness: I will go into them, and I will praise the Lord: This gate of the Lord, into which the righteous shall enter.”

The gate of the Most High into which the righteous shall enter is the straight gate. The righteous nation that keeps the truth is the remnant that keeps the commandments, and that is who enters the strong city whose walls and bulwarks are salvation.

precepts.text: The stone which the builders refused is become the head stone of the corner; this is the Most High's doing, and it is marvellous in our eyes.
precepts.point: Christ is also a sanctuary, a place of refuge and comfort from the world, from crime, hatred, and murder, and he gives our people a purpose, which is what everybody is looking for. Simeon said the child is set for the fall and rising again of many in Israel, and the "own" that received him not is the fall of the scribes, Sadducees, and chief priests.

note.label: Acts 4: The Stone the Builders Rejected

precepts.why:
Peter is quoting David: “The stone which the builders refused is become the head stone of the corner. This is the Lord’s doing; it is marvellous in our eyes.”

It was the builders' job to build and bind the nation, to raise up the tabernacle of David, to bind the brokenhearted and to feed the flock. But when the stone, Christ, came, jealousy and vainglory arose and they refused him. The Most High made the refused stone the head of the corner, and that is his doing, marvellous in our eyes.
